messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: 8 CUDA OOM events on runtime-serving-v2 across 3 nodes in us-east-1 in the last 5m. Autoscaler flapped once. Suspect: KV cache growth + allocator fragmentation. Creating incident INC-2026-412. @Maya K and @Aj Patel oncall.

Maya K: seeing it, joining. do we have a list of affected nodes?

Aj Patel: pulling node list now. looks like nvidia-gpu-12, nvidia-gpu-14, nvidia-gpu-18 saw repeated container restarts. memory usage trend shows steady climb over 36h, not spikes. link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/serve/kv-cache-usage?panelId=7

Alex S: posting logs from pod runtime-serving-v2-7f9c: ```
[2026-02-11T03:12:01Z] ERROR runtime: cuda runtime error (2): out of memory at alloc.cu:124
stack: runtime/allocator.go:312 -> paged_allocator.go:178 -> kv_cache.go:409
Evicted keys: 0/1024, free pages: 3/256
```

Devin R: that stack looks like allocator failing to find contiguous pages, fragmentation + KV growth. eviction isn't keeping up.

Maya K: immediate mitigation: start draining the most impacted nodes and bounce runtime pods on them to reclaim fragmented memory. Aj can you drain nvidia-gpu-18?

Aj Patel: `kubectl cordon nvidia-gpu-18 && kubectl drain nvidia-gpu-18 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` started. 

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy watcher: rolling restart initiated for runtime-serving-v2 in us-east-1 (strategy: staggered, batchSize=3).

Aj Patel: post-drain, restarted pods landed on nvidia-gpu-20/22 (less loaded). memory graphs showing a ~15% drop after restart.

Lina C: customer-impact check: CS dashboard shows ~120 failed requests (500s) in last 10m for accounts on dedicated capacity. Notified one major customer (AcmeCorp) about degraded performance.

Maya K: good catch. can we trigger a manual KV eviction for the biggest prefixes while we investigate root cause? runtime admin endpoint supports on-the-fly evict. Aj, Alex can you run eviction for large prefixes `model-cache/*` and `session-kv/*`?

Alex S: running: ```bash
curl -X POST 'https://runtime-admin.us-east-1.redwood/internal/evict' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' 
  -d '{"prefix":"model-cache/","max_keys":2000}'
```
Response: `{"evicted":1783, "freed_pages":12}`

Devin R: that freed some pages but allocator fragment map still shows many small free slices. I want to switch the allocator to coalesce mode to reduce fragmentation. That requires a flag flip in the runtime: `RW_ALLOC_COALESCE=true`. We can patch deployment with zero-downtime rollout.

Maya K: approve. Alex, push patch to runtime-config configmap with the flag and trigger a controlled restart (one pod at a time). Keep canary to 10%.

Alex S: patch applied, canary 1/10 restarted. Observing memory stabillization on canary pod.

Aj Patel: note — we hit a CUDA OOM inside attention paging path when sequence_len > 4096 combined with a cold KV cache fetch. stack points to paged_attention.go: `allocPageRange` failing. Might be a pathological workload (long sequences + many KV lookups).

Maya K: action: add temporary quota: reject requests with seq_len > 4096 on affected model variants and turn on soft-fallback to smaller context window. Devin, can you add a routing rule?

Devin R: done. `PATCH /routing/overrides` applied: models/*/v2 => if seq_len>4096 return 413 with suggestion to use truncated context or use model-xlarge-short.

Lina C: Updated customers: AcmeCorp saw intermittent 500s; they appreciate the proactive update. No major data loss. Logging suggests retries succeeded once pods moved.

Maya K: we're stabilizing. recording mitigations for handoff: 1) drained nvidia-gpu-18, 2) manual evict of `model-cache/*` and `session-kv/*`, 3) enable `RW_ALLOC_COALESCE=true` (canary rolling rollout), 4) added routing quota for seq_len.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary rollout completed successfully (10%). No regressions after 5m.

Aj Patel: memory slope flattened on canary and subsequent pods. still see low-level leak ~1-2% over 24h. likely separate leak in KV tombstone handling. adding a debug counter to count tombstones and eviction misses.

Devin R: created INC-2026-412-ROOT (tracking RCA). Owner: eng-runtime (Alex S). Timeline: immediate mitigations done, ongoing telemetry instrument, postmortem in 48h.

Maya K: handoff to next oncall @Aj Patel in 30m. please monitor AutoScale and the eviction metrics: `kv.evictions.rate`, `allocator.coalesce.ratio`, `cuda.oom.count`.

Aj Patel: ack. I'll keep an eye and escalate if `cuda.oom.count` > 2 in 10m.

Lina C: customer update posted to #customer-notifs. template used and sent to impacted accounts.

Maya K: notes for postmortem: investigate KV tombstone creation pattern after model updates, ensure eviction policy is aggressive enough for bursts, evaluate switching to larger base page size for paged allocator, and harden routes for large seq_len. Assign owners in the PM.

Alex S: uploading debug dump and fresh heap profile to the incident ticket. link: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/inc/INC-2026-412/heapdump.tgz

Devin R: follow-ups created: TASK-1468 (allocator: coalesce as default + configurable page_size), TASK-1469 (eviction prioritization by prefix + tombstone scavenger), TASK-1470 (add alerting on coalesce ratio drop).

Maya K: thanks team. handing off. leave any lingering notes here and I'll write the incident summary when I'm off. :white_check_mark: 

Aj Patel: here for next 45m. will post if anything spikes.

incident-bot: INC-2026-412 status -> mitigated (immediate actions applied). Severity: Sev2.

Maya K: closing chat for active handoff. please escalate to pager if any OOMs return.

Alex S: one last note — we saw one node with GPU driver `525.105.17` behaving marginally older; scheduling upgrade in maintenance window as precaution.

Devin R: noted. will add to postmortem runbook.

Lina C: closing customer comms loop after final verification.

Maya K: end.
